text:
eva: Quick flag from a customer onboarding call: their rerank results were misaligned after our retry logic kicked in. They had correct embeddings and scores but mismatch to queries.

omar: Can you share the sampleapp language + payload?

eva: Node sampleapp, batch helper set to maxChunk=1024. Sent three items: q-alpha, q-beta, q-gamma. They saw q-beta get q-alpha's vector. Logs show a 401 and immediate refresh.

sylvie: Same pattern we've seen: runtime splits across shards, retry appends the partial arrays instead of merging by id, and some shards route to quantized path which emits base64 fp16 under "embedding" while others use numeric array "vector".

omar: Ugh. That combination will absolutely break helpers that assume positional mapping.

eva: I've attached the captured body (redacted):
```json
{"results":[{"id":"q-beta","vector":[0.2,0.3,...],"dim":1536},{"id":"q-alpha","vector":[0.1,0.4,...],"dim":1536},{"id":"q-gamma","vector":[...],"dim":1536}]}
```
But the returned assembly on the client was [q-alpha,q-beta,q-gamma] because the helper mapped by index.

sylvie: Short-term mitigation: normalize responses by id client-side and accept both formats (numeric array and base64-encoded fp16). Example Python normalizer I pushed to the sampleapp repo: 
```py
def normalize_by_id(resp, items):
    by_id = {r['id']: r for r in resp['results']}
    out = []
    for it in items:
        e = by_id.get(it['id'])
        if e is None:
            raise ValueError(f"missing id {it['id']}")
        vec = e.get('vector')
        if vec is None and 'embedding' in e:
            vec = decode_fp16_base64(e['embedding'])
        out.append({'id': it['id'], 'vec': coerce_numeric(vec)})
    return out
```
This makes the client resistant to ordering and small schema drift.

omar: Nice. Can you add a tiny fuzz test that shuffles response order and also replaces one entry with an embedding b64?

sylvie: Done. I added a Jest/pytest fuzz that randomly permutes resp.results and toggles quantized format. It caught a couple of edgecases where the helper tried to Float32Array.from a list of strings.

eva: Platform suggestion: can we add a lightweight stable field on responses called "seq" or echo the incoming item-id per-entry so merge can be idempotent server-side? That would make client code simpler.

platform-bot: PLATFORM-1428 updated: agreed to add id echo in merged responses and a response header X-Embedding-Format indicating "float32" | "fp16-b64". ETA: next minor release.

omar: Nice. But we should not rely on the rollout to fix all user code. SDKs must be defensive. I'll open PRs for Node, Go, and Python helpers to always map by id and to normalize types. Also add conformance test that loads two fixtures: numeric-path.json and quantized-path.json and asserts identical in-memory vectors.

sylvie: One gotcha we found in the fuzz: dim mismatch. quantized path sometimes reports dim as a string ("768") while numeric path reports 1536. Helpers should validate dims and raise clear errors instead of silently coercing or assuming. Add ambiguity detections to onboarding docs.

eva: For onboarding docs I added a short checklist: 1) verify expected dim, 2) normalize by id, 3) coerce numeric types and decode b64, 4) fail loudly on missing ids. Also added a snippet showing defensive mapping.

omar: I'll land the helper PRs with tests today. sylvie can you paste the fuzz harness in the PR so QA can run it in CI?

sylvie: Yup. The harness simulates auth-refresh mid-batch, splits responses, and randomizes order and format. It found the mapping bug in the Node helper with just 200 iterations.

platform-bot: Note: deploy channel flagged PR #6480 that changes merge behavior. Keep an eye on canary.

eva: Great work. Once SDK PRs land we'll remove the flaky marker from the sampleapp tests. Thanks everyone. :party_popper:
